selected_problem: Fresh main made PR creation receipts addressable by a durable PR number, but the create step still posted only a branch name and did not bind the returned PR head to the exact validated commit. If the remote branch moved after exact-object push but before PR creation, the provider could accept a PR whose head no longer matched the validated candidate; the later merge expected-head gate would reject it, but PR-create itself would already have been falsely reported as a correct delivery step.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The new main left one narrow, deterministic and central artifact-binding gap at PR creation: the returned remote PR head was not checked against the already validated local commit. The singular evidence-rich bottleneck gate routes this replay to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt or fabricated numeric routing score is claimed.

pre_fix_reproduction.observation: gitRemoteDelivery pushed the exact expected commit, then called githubCreatePullRequest without expectedHeadSha; githubCreatePullRequest accepted any positive PR-number receipt and never inspected `response.head.sha`.
pre_fix_reproduction.consequence: A remote branch move between push and PR POST could yield a newly-created PR for a different head while the provider still reported the PR-create step as successful.

changes: githubCreatePullRequest now accepts an optional expectedHeadSha binding, resolves it to a concrete local commit before any GitHub PR-create side effect, and fails closed if that expected commit is invalid or unavailable.
When an expected head is supplied, a successful PR-create receipt must report `head.sha` equal to the resolved expected commit; mismatch fails with PR_CREATE_HEAD_MISMATCH.

If GitHub may already have created a mismatched PR, `prPerformed=true`, `externalSideEffectPerformed=true`, and the returned PR number/head are preserved so the external side effect remains traceable rather than being erased.
gitRemoteDelivery now forwards its already-authoritative expectedHeadSha into PR creation, binding the normal provider path from exact-object push through PR receipt.

commands: node --test exact candidate PR receipt + PR head focused tests
validation.tests: 5/5 PASS across 3 new head-binding cases plus the 2 previous PR-receipt cases
cases: created PR head differs from expected validated commit: rejected while preserving PR side-effect truth
created PR head equals expected validated commit: accepted
gitRemoteDelivery forwards expectedHeadSha to PR creation and rejects a moved head
previous missing-PR-number receipt regression remains passing
previous valid-PR-number receipt regression remains passing
validation.verification_note: The candidate core blob and new focused test blob were byte-identical to the locally executed files; the combined focused harness passed 5/5. No GitHub Actions were used.

truth_boundaries: This verifies the PR head after GitHub creates the PR; GitHub's create-PR endpoint still has no caller-supplied atomic expected-head-SHA precondition, so a moved branch may still cause an unwanted PR side effect before the mismatch is observed.
The later merge expected-head precondition prevents the mismatched PR head from being silently merged.
The GitHub merge endpoint still lacks a caller-supplied expected-base-SHA precondition, so base movement remains a separate unresolved integration-boundary problem.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is introduced.
